posts.author: vinoodd
posts.content_md:
Dear Sirs,

I work in a firm which manufactures Optics & Opto mechanical components in India. We are in a state of developing Holography Kits & introduce them to all the Universities & Colleges in India.

The only bottle neck we find is that in the case of Holography plates, which has to import everytime with the supply which makes the Kit costlier. 

Any body has any suggestions in which we can develop some plates in which we can record holograms?

The experiment we are hoping to introduce is grating devlopement and calculation of its spacing. So life time of the plate is not that important, ie we may need max upto 3 months.

Please email me your valuable suggestions regarding this,

Vinod.R

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md:
I suggest you try to find a local source for your plates in each country. You can rely on their process control to provide consistent results, while you concentrate on you own value added component. I've had trouble getting plates shipped into the US getting fogged by security X-ray inspection. 

There are several sources of plates and film around the world:

[http://www.holokits.com/](http://www.holokits.com/)

[http://www.vinteq.com/](http://www.vinteq.com/)

[http://www.geola.com/](http://www.geola.com/)

[http://www.ultimate-holography.com/](http://www.ultimate-holography.com/)

[http://polarisresearchgroup.com/](http://polarisresearchgroup.com/)

and from elsewhere in this forum

> Colourholographics Ltd is a manufacturer and supplier of the BB range of emulsions. We manufacture ultra fine grain red, green and blue sensitive plates in a variety of sizes, from 2.5"x2.5" to 50x60cm.If you send me an email I can send you all the information about our emulsions, including an updated price list and processing information.Manuel UlibarrenaColour Holographic LtdUnit 3, Heybridge House Industrial EstateThe Causeway, Maldon, Essex, CM9 4XLemail: manuel at colourholographic dot com

...and of course the newcomer, Fuji.

posts.author: Sergio
posts.content_md: .......another option is the Polygrama photopolymer, that indeed the dry coated material is an excellent option to make low cost educational plates since it does not require development, can make high DE transmission and reflection gratings and fairly better to coat than gelatin. Sensitivity is below 1mJ/cm² range now.

posts.content_md:
> **vinoodd:** Any body has any suggestions in which we can develop some plates in which we can record holograms?

If you mean make your own plates when you use "develop" in the above quote, then search this site for DCG and Silver Halide Emulsion Fabrication. Then you can make your own. Cost is low but your time is needed.
